 European Retailers Expand Private-Label Cosmetics Made in Korea
Mercadona and Ulta Beauty Sell Korean-Made Products
Japanese and Brazilian Drugmakers Partner With Korean Manufacturers
Top Three ODM Firms Boost Plant Investment on Export Growth
 Business | Published 2026.11.16. 07:00:05 | By Kang Dong-heon kaaangs10@sedaily.com | Summary | Save A A A Photo courtesy of Cosmax Overseas retailers are no longer content to simply stock Korean beauty brands — a growing number are having their own private-label products made in South Korea. European drugstores and supermarkets, along with foreign pharmaceutical companies, are increasingly partnering with Korean cosmetics manufacturers. As K-beauty's global profile rises, more overseas firms are looking to tap Korea's product development and production capabilities.
 Kruidvat, a drugstore chain operating more than 1,250 stores in the Netherlands and Belgium, launched its own brand "Kruidvat Korean Skincare" in June with eight Korean-made skincare products, according to the beauty industry on the 15th. Kruidvat, which had introduced Korean cosmetics brands such as Beauty of Joseon and SKIN1004 to local consumers, has now begun selling Korean-made cosmetics under its own label.
 German drugstore chain Rossmann added eight skincare products developed and produced in Korea to ISANA, a brand known for value-for-money cosmetics, in October last year. Mercadona, Spain's largest supermarket operator, introduced Korean-made PDRN and collagen eye patches under its private label Deliplus in August, and expanded the lineup last month with a "K-Skin" range that includes a PDRN serum and gel cream. U.S. beauty retailer Ulta Beauty is also selling Korean-made eye patches under its own Ulta Beauty Collection brand, starting at $8.
 Foreign pharmaceutical companies are partnering with Korean manufacturers as well. Genecell, the Korean unit of Japanese drug distributor Alfresa Group, signed a contract with Cosmax in September to develop and produce premium skincare products. The products use stem cell culture supernatant, combining Japanese ingredient technology with Korean manufacturing capabilities.
 Brazilian pharmaceutical giant Cimed is also using Korea as a cosmetics production base. Cimed has invested 80 million reais (about 18.9 billion won) to develop the skincare brand Mili with Korea's GDK Cosmetics. Seven products have been developed and produced so far, with a target of 100 by the end of 2027.
 Amid rising demand for cosmetics manufacturing aimed at overseas markets, export results at South Korea's major original design manufacturing (ODM) firms are also growing. Cosmax's export revenue rose about 1.7-fold to 450.5 billion won in 2025 from 263.6 billion won in 2022. Over the same period, Kolmar Korea's export revenue grew 2.2-fold to 90.6 billion won from 41.9 billion won, while Cosmecca Korea's rose 2.5-fold to 73 billion won from 28.9 billion won.
 Cosmecca Korea has accordingly spent 200 billion won to build a new production facility in Ochang, North Chungcheong Province. Cosmax plans to expand output by investing 60.5 billion won in an extension of its plant in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province. "Kolmar Korea will see its capacity expand when its Sejong plant comes online next year, allowing it to absorb 30% revenue growth for at least the next three years," said Kim Myung-joo, an analyst at Korea Investment & Securities. "Cosmax also takes three to four months to develop and produce a product, shorter than global rivals at five to eight months, giving it an edge in a global cosmetics market where speed to launch matters."
